//: Cases every capacity evaluator must answer the same way. Expected values are worked by hand from the rule (each why says how), never copied from an evaluator. Format: README.md beside this file.

vectors.name: measured host: one light agent
vectors.why: Design section 3 worked example; the design rounds the margin to 1208, the rule rounds it up to 1209.

vectors.name: measured host: today's ceiling of 10 agents
vectors.why: 8 agents alive, the default ceiling stops the third new one.

vectors.name: incident fan-out of 24 light agents
vectors.why: A 24-run fan-out filled swap: each new agent counts at 384 MB from second zero; with the ceiling lifted 10 of 24 fit (4147/384), the rest wait.

vectors.name: measured host: 2 builds
vectors.why: 4147 MB free holds two 2048 MB builds.

vectors.name: measured host: 1 build then 5 light agents
vectors.why: 4147-2048=2099 MB holds 5 more light agents.

vectors.name: total grows to 18 GB: builds stop at 4 by cores
vectors.why: Total read live: margin 1844, free 14326-1844-906-1715=9861. 4 builds use 10.0 of 10.8 job cores; a fifth would pass 90% of 12 cores.

vectors.name: total grows to 18 GB: writers follow job room
vectors.why: Idle room 14326+2627-1844-1715=13394 MB holds 6 builds, cores 4, so at most 2x4=8 writers.

vectors.name: total shrinks to 10 GB
vectors.why: The host takes RAM back: margin 1024, free 6134-1024-906-1715=2489: one build, or 6 light agents.

vectors.name: total shrinks to 10 GB: light agents
vectors.why: 2489/384 = 6 light agents.

vectors.name: incident: 18 build agents and a test server at once
vectors.why: 18 build-running agents plus a test server filled swap. Writers stop at 8 (idle room 9391 holds 4 builds), then 1 build fits, the 4608 MB server does not. Admitted 8x768+2048=8192 <= 9391.

vectors.name: incident: two CI runs and an agent build on 12 cores
vectors.why: With start costs all three builds fit: 3 x 250 = 750 of the 1080 job centi-cores, 6144 of 9391 MB. The start cost alone does not refuse this incident (the measured build cost is 1.6-2.5 cores). The protection: all three now ask one rule (before, two ran outside any door); a build that uses more CPU learns it (next vector refuses it); jobs keep a low CPU weight (outside the rule).

vectors.name: incident: two CI runs and an agent build, builds that learned 6 cores
vectors.why: The protection against the load-90 incident: builds that learned 6 cores (600 centi-cores, inside 400% of 250). The first uses 600 of the 1080 job centi-cores; the second would make 1200 > 1080, so it and the third wait for cores. The job floor (1) is already met.

vectors.name: incident: CI runs and a build on 4 cores
vectors.why: On 4 cores (3.6 for jobs) the second build waits for cores.

vectors.name: incident: a capped box stalls while the machine has free memory
vectors.why: The build box stalls at its cap (box PSI full 15%) while the machine reads PSI 0 and has 9391 MB free. The level takes the worst of machine and box: severe, so nothing more goes into that box, floors included.

vectors.name: machine stall with a calm box is still severe
vectors.why: Machine PSI full 15%, the box reads 0: the worst of the two is severe, nothing new.

vectors.name: box PSI elevated, machine calm
vectors.why: Box PSI some 12% (limit 10%) with a calm machine: elevated. The job floor admits one build (10600-2048=8552 stays above the severe line 604.5); the second is refused as elevated.

vectors.name: box PSI unreadable is elevated
vectors.why: A box PSI that could not be read is never ok: elevated, and the 8 live agents are above the floor.

vectors.name: a box that is not calm keeps elevated
vectors.why: Machine calm, box PSI some 7% (under the elevated 10%, above the calm 5%): the 60 s wait does not start.

vectors.name: incident: a leftover build daemon
vectors.why: An unknown tenant (a daemon left after a build) holds 2500 MB: it is already out of available memory, nobody lists it. 3 builds fit, not 4.

vectors.name: finding: per-box caps add up past RAM; one budget does not
vectors.why: Every kind is charged to one budget: 8 writers, 1 build, 1 test run; 8960 of 9391 MB.

vectors.name: 8 GB laptop, basic tier: wider margin
vectors.why: No per-piece caps: margin 1024x1.5=1536, free 4064: 10 light agents.

vectors.name: 8 GB laptop: writers follow job room
vectors.why: Idle room 4064 holds 1 build, so writers stop at the minimum of 2; then 1 build.

vectors.name: machine smaller than the floor: writers
vectors.why: Floor of 2 agents, but the second writer would take available-owed to 64 MB, under the severe line (768): physical memory wins.

vectors.name: machine smaller than the floor: light agents
vectors.why: Two light agents keep 832 MB, above the severe line: the floor of 2 holds.

vectors.name: machine smaller than the floor, already elevated
vectors.why: 1100 MB available is under the margin (elevated); a writer would leave 332 MB, under the severe line: nothing starts.

vectors.name: one job always runs on a small CPU
vectors.why: 2.5 cores allow 2.25 for jobs, a build needs 2.5: the job floor admits one, the second waits for cores.

vectors.name: a ceiling under the floor wins
vectors.why: Ceilings are absolute: with a ceiling of 1 agent the floor of 2 does not apply.

vectors.name: reservation larger than the machine
vectors.why: 20000 MB held on a 12 GB machine: nothing above the floors; floors ignore reservations but not the severe line.

vectors.name: reservation larger than the machine, agents above the floor
reservation partly used
vectors.why: Held 1715, holder uses 700: 1015 still reserved.

vectors.name: reservation with unknown or broken use holds it all
vectors.why: useMb null, negative or larger than the machine counts as 0 used; a negative reservation holds nothing.

vectors.name: owed growth larger than available
vectors.why: 6 writers and 2 builds just admitted owe 8704 MB, more than the 7977 available: free -3651, nothing starts.

vectors.name: a piece that has grown owes nothing
vectors.why: A build at 2500 MB demand is past its 2048 cost: owed 0.

vectors.name: empty state: no pieces, no reservations key
vectors.why: A fresh machine with nothing running.

vectors.name: total in bytes
vectors.why: 12 GB given in bytes as MB is above the bound: unreadable, never free.

vectors.name: total in KB
vectors.why: 12 GB given in kB as MB (12372992) is above the 1048575 MB bound: unreadable.

vectors.name: total in GB
vectors.why: 12 given as MB is below the 1024 MB bound: unreadable.

vectors.name: 2 GB box read in kB
vectors.why: /proc/meminfo is in kB: a 2 GB box read as MB says 2097152, above the 1048575 MB bound. Unreadable: nothing admitted (read right, the same box admits 1 writer).

vectors.name: 4 GB box read in kB
vectors.why: 4096 MB in kB is 4194304, above the 1048575 MB bound: unreadable.

vectors.name: 1 GB read in kB, or 1 TiB of RAM: unreadable
vectors.why: 1048576 is above the 1048575 MB bound. It is a 1 GB machine read in kB, or a machine with 1 TiB of RAM: the rule cannot tell them apart, so it takes the safe side (unreadable). Such a big machine raises maxTotalMb in its rule file.

vectors.name: largest readable machine
machine under 1 GB is unreadable
vectors.why: 1000 MB total is below the 1024 MB bound (also what a 1 TB machine read in GB looks like); the minimum margin alone is 1024 MB, so nothing could run.

vectors.name: cores in centi-cores
vectors.why: 12 cores given as 1200 (hundredths) is above the 1024-core bound: unreadable.

vectors.name: swap in kB is unreadable
vectors.why: 4 GB of swap given in kB (4194304) is above the 1048575 MB bound: swap unreadable, so elevated and the wider margin ceil(120830 x 150 / 10000) = 1813. Nothing runs, so the floor admits (10600-384 = 10216 >= 906.5).

vectors.name: reservation in bytes holds at most the largest machine
vectors.why: 1 GB held, given in bytes (1073741824), counts as 1048575 MB (the bound), so sums stay exact in every language. free 10600-1209-1048575 = -1039184: only the floor admits.

vectors.name: available in bytes
vectors.why: Available above total is impossible: unreadable.

vectors.name: available negative
vectors.why: Available below 0 is impossible: unreadable, never free.

vectors.name: total missing
vectors.why: No total means nothing is known: unreadable, never "no limit".

vectors.name: total not a number
vectors.why: A string is not a number, even when it reads like one: unreadable.

vectors.name: cores zero
vectors.why: 0 cores is impossible: unreadable.

vectors.name: pieces unreadable
vectors.why: A failed list of live pieces never means none are running.

vectors.name: reservations not a list
vectors.why: A broken reservation list is not ignored.

vectors.name: unreadable keeps severe
vectors.why: An unreadable read never lowers the level.

vectors.name: available zero is a reading
vectors.why: 0 MB available is real: severe.

vectors.name: demand in bytes is not trusted
vectors.why: A demand larger than the machine counts as 0: the piece owes in full (906+209).

vectors.name: negative or missing demand owes in full
vectors.why: Demand -1 and no demand both count as 0: each writer owes 768, owed 1536, free 10600-1209-1536=7855.

vectors.name: declared size in bytes falls back
vectors.why: A test server declaring 4 GiB in bytes is above the bound: the 4096 MB fallback plus 512.

vectors.name: declared size
vectors.why: A test server with a 2048 MB heap costs 2560 MB.

vectors.name: fractional available rounds down
margin exact at 10%
vectors.why: 12080 MB total: margin 1208 exactly.

vectors.name: margin rounds up
vectors.why: 12081 MB total: 1208.1 rounds up to 1209.

vectors.name: fractional demand rounds down
vectors.why: A demand of 209.9 counts as 209: owed stays 906.

vectors.name: no swap widens the margin
vectors.why: Margin 1209 x1.5 = 1812.45, rounded up to 1813.

vectors.name: no per-piece caps widens the margin
zero swap is no swap
vectors.why: Swap total 0 is no swap: wider margin 1813, and no swap-free limit, so the level stays ok.

vectors.name: elevated by memory stall with free memory
vectors.why: PSI some 12%: no new piece above the floors, though 4147 MB are free.

vectors.name: elevated: floors still start
vectors.why: With nothing running the floors (2 agents) still start while elevated.

vectors.name: elevated at the PSI full limit
vectors.why: full avg10 2% is the limit (>=).

vectors.name: just under the PSI some limit
vectors.why: 9.99% is ok.

vectors.name: elevated by swap nearly full
vectors.why: 600 of 4096 MB swap free is under 15%, and it fell from 800 MB at the last read: by 200 MB, more than swapFillingMb (64), so swap is filling.

vectors.name: full swap of cold pages is not a signal
vectors.why: 600 of 4096 MB swap free (under 15%) but 600 MB at the last read too: nothing is being pushed out, so not elevated, and calm: the 60 s wait since 1000000 ms has passed, so ok.

vectors.name: swap trend not known yet keeps the wait but never ends it
vectors.why: Previous state without a swap read (a restart): the swap trend is unknown. The read is otherwise calm, so the 60 s wait (since 1000000) goes on, but it ends only on a read that can see whether swap is filling: still elevated at 60 s.

vectors.name: swap filling is never calm
vectors.why: Swap free 2150 MB, 2300 MB at the last read: it fell by 150 MB, more than swapFillingMb (64). Above 15% free, so not elevated by swap, but not calm: the wait starts over.

vectors.name: swap shrinking by the filling limit is not filling
vectors.why: Swap free 2150 MB, 2214 MB at the last read: it fell by exactly swapFillingMb (64), which is not more than it, so calm and ok after the 60 s wait.

vectors.name: severe by memory stall with free memory
vectors.why: PSI full 10%: nothing new, floors included.

vectors.name: severe by available under half the margin
vectors.why: 600 MB available < 1209/2.

vectors.name: elevated by available under the margin
vectors.why: 1200 MB available < 1209.

vectors.name: PSI unreadable is elevated
vectors.why: A PSI file that could not be read is never "ok": elevated, and 8 agents are above the floor.

vectors.name: PSI out of range is unreadable
vectors.why: PSI is a percentage 0-100; -1 is broken, so elevated.

vectors.name: swap unreadable is elevated and widens the margin
vectors.why: Unreadable swap counts as no swap for the margin (1813) and as elevated for the level.

vectors.name: swap free above total is unreadable
vectors.why: 200 MB free of 100 MB swap is impossible: elevated.

vectors.name: no PSI: OS level severe
vectors.why: A machine without PSI uses its OS pressure level.

vectors.name: no PSI: OS level garbage is unreadable
vectors.why: An OS level that is not ok, elevated or severe is broken: elevated.

vectors.name: elevated to ok waits: calm starts
vectors.why: Calm readings after elevated start the 60 s wait. Swap free is 2150 MB as at the last read: not filling.

vectors.name: elevated to ok waits: 59.999 s
vectors.why: Calm since 1000000 ms, now 1059999: 59.999 s is under the 60 s wait, so still elevated and the calm start is kept.

vectors.name: elevated to ok after 60 s
vectors.why: Calm since 1000000 ms, now 1060000: 60 s of calm readings, so ok again and the calm start is cleared.

vectors.name: not calm restarts the wait
vectors.why: PSI some 7% is under the limit but above half of it.

vectors.name: severe steps down after 120 s
vectors.why: No severe reading since 1000000 ms, now 1120000: 120 s, so one step down to elevated (not to ok).

vectors.name: severe waits 119.999 s
vectors.why: 119.999 s is under the 120 s wait: still severe.

vectors.name: severe stays while severe
vectors.why: 500 MB available is under half the margin (604.5): severe again, so the wait starts over (calmSinceMs null).

vectors.name: up at once
vectors.why: PSI full 2% is the elevated limit: up from ok on the first such read, no wait.

vectors.name: clock went back restarts the wait
vectors.why: Now (1000000) is before the calm start (2000000): the clock went back, so the wait restarts from now.

vectors.name: no clock never steps down
vectors.why: Without nowMs the rule cannot know how long it was calm: it stays elevated.

vectors.name: no previous state takes the raw level
vectors.why: First read or restart.

vectors.name: unknown job kind is the expensive default
vectors.why: A job kind from a newer build counts as 3072 MB.

vectors.name: unknown or empty kind is a writer
vectors.why: Nothing said = writer: unknown is expensive.

vectors.name: unlabelled live pieces count as writers
vectors.why: After a restart unlabelled agents owe the writer cost.

vectors.name: one type-check at a time
vectors.why: A type-check is already running and the kind allows 1 at once: refused by the kind limit.

vectors.name: learned cost is clamped up to 4x
vectors.why: A learned 99999 MB writer counts as 3072 MB, for the two live writers too: owed 6144.

vectors.name: learned cost is clamped down to half
vectors.why: A learned 10 MB writer counts as at least 50% of 768 = 384 MB.

vectors.name: broken learned cost is the start cost
vectors.why: A negative learned cost is broken: the 768 MB start cost.

vectors.name: agreement: cores true is unreadable
vectors.why: A boolean is not a number (Python's bool is an int: a lax evaluator reads true as 1 core).

vectors.name: agreement: total true is unreadable
vectors.why: A boolean total is not a number: unreadable.

vectors.name: agreement: demand true owes in full
vectors.why: A boolean demand is broken, so 0: the light agent owes 384 (a lax evaluator says 383). free 10600-1209-384 = 9007.

vectors.name: agreement: reservation use true holds it all
vectors.why: A boolean use is broken, so 0 used: 1000 reserved (a lax evaluator says 999).

vectors.name: agreement: reservation size true holds nothing
vectors.why: A boolean size is broken: it holds 0 (a lax evaluator holds 1).

vectors.name: agreement: swap free true is unreadable
vectors.why: Boolean swap free: swap unreadable, so elevated and the wider margin 1813; nothing runs, so the floor admits.

vectors.name: agreement: PSI true is unreadable
vectors.why: A boolean PSI value is broken: elevated; nothing runs, so the floor admits.

vectors.name: agreement: declared size true falls back
vectors.why: A boolean declared size is broken: the 4096 MB fallback plus 512.

vectors.name: agreement: learned cost true is the start cost
vectors.why: A boolean learned cost is broken: the 768 MB start cost (a lax evaluator clamps 1 up to 384).

vectors.name: agreement: whole numbers written with a fraction
vectors.why: 12083.0 is 12083 and count 2.0 is 2 in every evaluator (a JSON parser may give a float): margin 1209, both light agents admitted.

vectors.name: a bad learned cost cannot lock the floor
vectors.why: On a small machine the learned 3072 does not fit, but the floor counts the 768 start cost.

vectors.name: learned cores change the core check
vectors.why: Builds that learned 1 core: 10 fit the cores, memory stops them at 4.

vectors.name: job ceiling
vectors.why: Today's 4 jobs.

vectors.name: job core share: default jobs on 2.78 cores
vectors.why: 2.78 cores are 278 centi-cores, 90% of them 250: one default job (250 centi-cores) fits exactly, a second would need 500. The job floor is 0 here, so it does not admit the second either.

vectors.name: job core share: servers on 1.12 cores
vectors.why: 1.12 cores are 112 centi-cores, 90% of them 100: one server (100 centi-cores) fits exactly, a second would need 200.

vectors.name: job core share: a typecheck on 0.34 cores with its cost free exactly
vectors.why: 0.34 cores are 34 centi-cores, 90% of them 30: a typecheck (30 centi-cores) fits exactly. Margin 1209, so 4281 MB available leave 3072 MB free: its whole start cost. One more centi-core or MB and it waits (job floor 0 here).

vectors.name: calm needs available at 150% of the margin
vectors.why: Margin 1209: calm needs 1813.5 MB available, so 1813 MB is not calm (though above the elevated line, the margin): after elevated the 60 s wait does not start.

vectors.name: #800: a job owes its declared size when that is more than its kind's cost
vectors.why: Margin 1209, available 10600. The test job declared 4000 MB (heavy's reservation for it) and uses 100: it owes 4000 - 100 = 3900, not 768 - 100 = 668. Free 10600 - 1209 - 3900 = 5491.

vectors.name: #800: a declared size below the kind's cost changes nothing
vectors.why: A build that declared 1000 MB still owes its kind's 2048 (a floor, never a cap). Free 10600 - 1209 - 2048 = 7343.

vectors.name: #800: an impossible declared size is no floor
vectors.why: Declared true, 0 and 1048576 (above maxTotalMb) are not sizes: each build owes its kind's 2048. Owed 6144, free 10600 - 1209 - 6144 = 3247.

vectors.name: #800: a fractional declared size above the kind's cost rounds up
vectors.why: A test job (768 MB) declaring 4000.4 MB costs 4001: a declared size rounds up (never down to 4000).

vectors.name: #800: a declared size of exactly maxTotalMb is a floor
vectors.why: 1048575 is maxTotalMb itself: still a size (the bound is inclusive), so the test job costs 1048575 and free 9391 cannot hold it. Were the bound exclusive it would cost 768 and fit.

vectors.name: #800: a learned cost above the declared size wins
vectors.why: The build kind learned 6000 MB; the piece declared 3000: the cost is the larger, 6000. Free 10600 - 1209 - 6000 = 3391.

vectors.name: #800: an ask's declared size is its cost, past the learned bound too
vectors.why: An unknown job (job-default, 3072) that declares 13000 MB costs 13000, above 400% of 3072 (12288): a declared size is not a learned one and is not clamped. 13000 > free 9391: not fits; the job floor (none running) admits it only above the severe line: 10600 - 13000 < 0, so budget.

vectors.name: #800: a fill step's declared size is owed by each admitted piece
vectors.why: Free 9391. Test jobs that declare 3000 MB each (their kind costs 768): one, two and three fit (owed 9000 <= 9391 after the third, cores 3 x 170 = 510 <= 1080); a fourth would need 3000 with 391 free: budget.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: the minimum margin on a host under 10 GB
vectors.why: Total 8000: 10% is 800 MB, under margin.minMb 1024, so the margin is 1024 (swap and per-piece caps: no widening).

vectors.name: #800 both ways: a total of exactly minTotalMb is read
vectors.why: Total 1024 is not below readingBounds.minTotalMb (1024): readable. Margin max(1024, 102.4) = 1024.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: a total one under minTotalMb is unreadable
vectors.why: Total 1023 is below readingBounds.minTotalMb (1024): unreadable, no margin.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: exactly maxCpuCores cores are read
vectors.why: 1024 cores is not above readingBounds.maxCpuCores (1024): readable, margin 1209.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: one core over maxCpuCores is unreadable
vectors.why: 1025 cores is above readingBounds.maxCpuCores (1024): unreadable.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: a test job costs its start
vectors.why: No learned cost: a job-test costs its startMb, 768.

vectors.why: 5.56 cores: 556 centi-cores, 90% is 500 (floor of 500.4). Two builds need 2 x 250 = 500 <= 500; a third 750: cores. Memory holds three (6144 <= 9391).

vectors.name: #800 both ways: two builds one centi-core over the job cores
vectors.why: 5.55 cores: 555 centi-cores, 90% is 499 (floor of 499.5). The second build makes 500 > 499: cores (the floor of 1 job is met by the first).

vectors.name: #800 both ways: two test jobs exactly fill the job cores
vectors.why: 3.78 cores: 378 centi-cores, 90% is 340 (floor of 340.2). Two test jobs need 2 x 170 = 340 <= 340; a third 510: cores.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: two test jobs one centi-core over the job cores
vectors.why: 3.77 cores: 377 centi-cores, 90% is 339 (floor of 339.3). The second test job makes 340 > 339: cores.

vectors.name: #800 both ways: a job-typecheck one centi-core over the job cores
vectors.why: 3.1 cores: 310 centi-cores, 90% is 279. A build runs (250); a job-typecheck (30) makes 280 > 279: cores. Memory fits (the build owes 2048 of 9391).

vectors.name: #800 both ways: a job-default one centi-core over the job cores
vectors.why: 5.55 cores: 555 centi-cores, 90% is 499. A build runs (250); a job-default (250) makes 500 > 499: cores. Memory fits (the build owes 2048 of 9391).
